definition_zh: 电的；用电的；电动的；令人激动的
definition_en: relating to electricity itself, working by electricity, or filled with tense excitement
core_image: 指尖刚碰到门把手，啪地跳出一小簇火花
scene: 雨夜里电水壶的开关咔一跳，壶身安静下来，壶嘴的蒸汽慢慢散开。The electric kettle switched itself off with a click.
sceneCN: 这里 electric 是「用电的」（第 2 个义项：靠电力工作的器具）；句意是那只电水壶咔一声自动断电。

pos.zh: 电的；用电的；电动的；令人激动的

senses.title: Of electricity itself
senses.definition: relating to electricity as a physical force, as in current, charge or field
senses.definitionCN: 指作为物理力量的电，如电流、电荷、电场
senses.example: The electric charge built up on the dry cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 干燥的布上积聚起了电荷。
senses.why: Electric comes from amber, which when rubbed attracts things; the word first named that force itself.
senses.whyCN: electric 来自琥珀，摩擦后会吸东西；这个词最初指的就是那股力量本身。

senses.title: Working by electricity
senses.definition: of a machine or device, driven by electricity rather than by fuel or by hand
senses.definitionCN: 指机器或设备，由电力而非燃料或人力驱动
senses.example: The electric kettle switched itself off with a click.
senses.exampleCN: 那只电水壶咔一声自动断电。
senses.why: Once the force had a name, anything running on it was simply described with the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这股力量一旦有了名字，任何靠它运转的东西就用同一个形容词来描述。

senses.title: Tense with excitement
senses.definition: filled with a tense, exciting feeling, as if a current were running through it
senses.definitionCN: 充满紧张兴奋的感觉，仿佛有电流穿过
senses.example: The hall went electric when the band walked on.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队一上台，整个大厅就沸腾了。
senses.why: A shock runs through the body, so a crowd in suspense is described as carrying the same current.
senses.whyCN: 电击会穿过身体，于是屏息的人群也被说成带着同一股电流。

intro.en: Electric was coined in the seventeenth century from Latin electrum, amber, from Greek elektron, because rubbed amber attracts light objects.
intro.cn: electric 是十七世纪由拉丁语 electrum（琥珀）造出，源自希腊语 elektron，因为摩擦过的琥珀会吸起轻物。

items.en: Elektron meant amber, the fossil resin that first showed the effect.
items.cn: elektron 意为「琥珀」，就是最先显现这种效应的树脂化石。

items.en: Latin kept electrum for amber and for a pale gold alloy.
items.cn: 拉丁语用 electrum 指琥珀，也指一种淡金色的合金。

items.en: Seventeenth-century scientists formed electricus for the force shown by rubbed amber.
items.cn: 十七世纪科学家造出 electricus，指摩擦琥珀所显现的那股力。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective and applied it first to bodies that attract.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，最初用于会吸引轻物的物体。

items.en: Industry widened it to machines, and writers stretched it to excitement.
items.cn: 工业把它扩展到机器，作家又把它拉向情绪上的激动。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the electricity family; the near-meaning group separates electrical, electronic and electrifying.
note.cn: 形近组收 electricity 词族；近义组区分 electrical、electronic 与 electrifying。

entries.definition: Relating to electricity as a system or field of engineering, rather than to one device.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「与电有关的、电气的」，指系统或工程，而非单个器具。

entries.definition: The energy carried by moving charges, or the supply of it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电；电力」。

entries.definition: A person who installs and repairs electrical wiring.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电工」。

entries.definition: To charge with electricity, or to thrill suddenly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使带电；使震惊」。

entries.definition: Working by controlling tiny charged particles in circuits, as computers do.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电子的」，靠控制电路中的带电微粒工作。

entries.definition: Extremely exciting; the feeling sense pushed to its strongest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「极其震撼的」，把情绪义推到最强。

entries.definition: Driven by a stated source, as in battery-powered.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「以……为动力的」，需说明动力来源。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with amber and a spark, then run the same current through kettles and through a crowd.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从琥珀与火花出发，再让同一股电流通过水壶与人群。

normal.en: Electric comes from amber: rub it and it pulls threads toward it.
normal.cn: electric 来自琥珀：摩擦之后它会把细线吸过来。

normal.en: Electric names the force; electrical names the system built around it.
normal.cn: electric 指那股力本身；electrical 指围绕它建立的系统。

normal.en: An electric kettle has a plug; an electrical fault has a cause.
normal.cn: electric kettle 有插头；electrical fault 有原因。

normal.en: A hall can go electric without a single wire.
normal.cn: 大厅可以一根电线也没有却「带电」。

normal.en: Electronic is one step further: not just current, but circuits controlling it.
normal.cn: electronic 再进一步：不只是电流，而是控制电流的电路。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip an inch from a door handle, a spark about to jump.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖离门把手一寸，火花就要跳过去。

abstract.en: The same jump can power a kettle or run through a waiting audience.
abstract.cn: 同一次跳跃可以带动水壶，也可以穿过等待的观众。

abstract.en: Electric is energy looking for somewhere to go.
abstract.cn: electric 就是一股急着找去处的能力。

examples.en: The electric charge built up on the dry cloth.
examples.cn: 干燥的布上积聚起了电荷。

examples.en: The electric kettle switched itself off with a click.
examples.cn: 那只电水壶咔一声自动断电。

examples.en: The hall went electric when the band walked on.
examples.cn: 乐队一上台，整个大厅就沸腾了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊莱克垂克」——指尖碰到门把手，啪地跳出火花

root: 源自希腊语 elektron「琥珀」→ 拉丁语 electrum → 近代拉丁语 electricus；因摩擦琥珀会吸轻物，十七世纪以此命名「电」这股力。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of electric: the physical force itself, devices driven by it, and a mood charged like a current.
sensesIntro.cn: electric 的三个义项：电这股物理力量本身、靠它驱动的器具，以及像电流一样紧绷的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spark jumping from a fingertip to a door handle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一簇火花从指尖跳到门把手上。

branches.en: THE FORCE: current, charge and field as physics names them.
branches.cn: 力量线：物理学所说的电流、电荷与电场。

branches.en: THE DEVICE: a kettle or car that runs on that force.
branches.cn: 器具线：靠这股力运转的水壶或汽车。

branches.en: THE MOOD: a crowd charged like a wire.
branches.cn: 情绪线：人群像导线一样带电。

branches.en: THE SUPPLY: the force and the things it drives are one circuit.
branches.cn: 供给线：力量与它驱动的东西是同一条回路。

branches.en: THE SWITCH: a device turns on, and so does a room.
branches.cn: 开关线：器具被打开，房间也被打开。

intro.en: Electric is a scientific coinage on Greek amber; English adds -ity, -al, -ian, -fy and -onic.
intro.cn: electric 是建立在希腊语「琥珀」上的科学造词；英语再加 -ity、-al、-ian、-fy 与 -onic。

latinIntro.en: Greek elektron and Latin electrum are recorded; electricus is a modern scientific formation, not an ancient word.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 elektron 与拉丁语 electrum 均有记录；electricus 是近代科学造词，不是古语。

items.example: It is the ultimate source of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是整个词族的最终来源。

items.example: It carried the Greek word into Latin.
items.exampleCN: 它把希腊词带入拉丁语。

items.example: It was coined in the seventeenth century.

definition_zh: 电的；与电有关的；电气的；用电的
definition_en: relating to electricity as a system, to electrical engineering, or to equipment that runs on electricity
core_image: 配电箱盖一打开，一排排彩色线束和标签露出来
scene: 电工掀开墙上的盖板，露出一排烧焦的线头，火就是从这一处线路故障烧起来的。An electrical fault had started the fire.
sceneCN: 这里 electrical 是「与电有关的、电气的」（第 1 个义项：指电力系统与线路，而非单个电器）；句意是线路中一处电气故障引发了火灾。

pos.zh: 电的；与电有关的；电气的；用电的

senses.title: Relating to electrical systems
senses.definition: relating to electricity as a system of supply, wiring and engineering
senses.definitionCN: 指作为供电、布线与工程系统的电
senses.example: She studied electrical engineering at college.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学学的是电气工程。
senses.why: The -al ending turns the noun electricity into a word about the field as a whole, so it suits systems rather than single devices.
senses.whyCN: -al 词尾把名词 electricity 变成指整个领域的词，因此它适合系统而不适合单个器具。

senses.title: Running on electricity
senses.definition: of equipment or appliances, operated by electricity, used as a general classifying word
senses.definitionCN: 指设备或器具由电力驱动，用作一般分类的说法
senses.example: Old electrical appliances use far more power.
senses.exampleCN: 旧家用电器耗电多得多。
senses.why: A whole class of goods is sorted by what drives them, so the classifying adjective takes the -al form.
senses.whyCN: 一整类商品按驱动方式分类，于是这个分类形容词采用了 -al 形式。

senses.title: Of the theory of electricity
senses.definition: relating to the scientific study of electricity and its properties
senses.definitionCN: 指对电及其性质的科学理论研究
senses.example: The paper compares the electrical properties of the two metals.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文比较了两种金属的电学性质。
senses.why: Properties belong to the science rather than to a machine, so the academic sense also takes -al.
senses.whyCN: 性质属于科学而不属于某台机器，所以学术义也用 -al 形式。

intro.en: Electrical is electric plus the Latin adjective ending -al; the stem goes back through Latin electrum to Greek elektron, amber.
intro.cn: electrical 是 electric 加拉丁语形容词词尾 -al；词干经拉丁语 electrum 上溯到希腊语 elektron（琥珀）。

items.en: Elektron meant amber, the substance that first showed the effect.
items.cn: elektron 意为「琥珀」，是最先显现这种效应的物质。

items.en: Seventeenth-century science coined electricus for the force amber shows.
items.cn: 十七世纪科学造出 electricus，指琥珀所显现的那股力。

items.en: English took the adjective and used it for bodies that attract and repel.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，用于相互吸引与排斥的物体。

items.en: The -al form was added to speak of the whole field rather than one object.
items.cn: 加上 -al 的形式用来谈整个领域，而不是单个物体。

items.en: Engineering, wiring and appliances settled into the -al branch, leaving electric for the vivid and the specific.
items.cn: 工程、布线与家电固定在 -al 这一支，把 electric 留给更具体、更生动的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the electricity family; the near-meaning group separates electric, electronic and powered.
note.cn: 形近组收 electricity 词族；近义组区分 electric、electronic 与 powered。

entries.definition: Of electricity itself, or of one device that runs on it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电的；用电的」，多指力量本身或单个器具。

entries.definition: The energy of moving charges, or its supply to homes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电；电力」。

entries.definition: By means of electricity, or in electrical terms.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「用电力地；在电气方面」。

entries.definition: A tradesperson who fits and repairs wiring.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电工」。

entries.definition: Working through circuits that control electrons, as phones and computers do.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电子的」，靠控制电子的电路工作，如手机与电脑。

entries.definition: Driven by a named source, such as solar-powered.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「以……为动力的」，须说明来源。

entries.definition: The public supply of electricity to a building.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「市电、供电网」，是 electrical 系统的来源。

normalIntro.en: These hooks open a fuse box, then draw the line between a single device and the whole system behind it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子打开一个配电箱，再划清「单个器具」与「背后整套系统」的界线。

normal.en: The -al makes it about the field: electrical engineering, electrical fault.
normal.cn: -al 让它指向整个领域：电气工程、电气故障。

normal.en: An electric kettle is one object; electrical wiring is the system feeding it.
normal.cn: electric kettle 是一件东西；electrical wiring 是给它供电的系统。

normal.en: Electrical appliances as a class, not one appliance in the hand.
normal.cn: electrical appliances 指一整类，而不是手里那一件。

normal.en: Electrical properties belong to the science, not to the plug.
normal.cn: electrical properties 属于科学，而不属于插头。

normal.en: Electric can thrill; electrical stays technical.
normal.cn: electric 可以令人激动；electrical 始终偏技术。

abstract.en: Picture the inside of a fuse box, rows of coloured wires and labels.
abstract.cn: 想象配电箱内部，一排排彩色导线与标签。

abstract.en: The same current that lights a lamp also has a name as a system.
abstract.cn: 点亮灯泡的那股电流，作为系统另有一个名称。

abstract.en: Electrical is the map; electric is the spark on it.
abstract.cn: electrical 是地图；electric 是地图上那颗火花。

examples.en: She studied electrical engineering at college.
examples.cn: 她在大学学的是电气工程。

examples.en: Old electrical appliances use far more power.
examples.cn: 旧家用电器耗电多得多。

examples.en: The paper compares the electrical properties of the two metals.
examples.cn: 这篇论文比较了两种金属的电学性质。

root: 由 electric 加拉丁语形容词词尾 -al 构成；electric 源自希腊语 elektron「琥珀」，经拉丁语 electrum 与近代拉丁语 electricus 而来。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of electrical: the supply system, equipment classified by its power source, and the science of electricity.
sensesIntro.cn: electrical 的三个义项：供电与线路系统、按动力分类的电器，以及电学理论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open fuse box with rows of coloured wires and labels.
core.cn: 核心意象：打开的配电箱，成排彩色导线与标签。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: supply, wiring and the engineering that runs them.
branches.cn: 系统线：供电、布线以及管理它们的工程。

branches.en: THE CLASS: appliances sorted by what drives them.
branches.cn: 分类线：按驱动方式归类的一整批电器。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE: properties studied rather than used.
branches.cn: 科学线：被研究而非被使用的性质。

branches.en: THE SUPPLY: the system and the goods it feeds form one grid.
branches.cn: 供给线：系统与它供养的电器构成一张电网。

branches.en: THE THEORY: every fault is a lesson in the science.
branches.cn: 理论线：每一次故障都是科学的一课。

intro.en: Electrical is electric plus the Latin adjective -al; the whole branch stays close to the Greek word for amber.
intro.cn: electrical 是 electric 加拉丁语形容词词尾 -al；整支词都与希腊语「琥珀」保持很近的距离。

latinIntro.en: Greek elektron and Latin electrum are recorded; electricus and the -al form are later scientific constructions.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 elektron 与拉丁语 electrum 有记录；electricus 与加 -al 的形式则是后来的科学构造。

definition_zh: 电；电能；电力供应；电学；（紧张兴奋的）气氛
definition_en: the energy carried by moving electric charges, the supply of such energy to buildings, the science that studies it, or a feeling of tense excitement in a crowd
core_image: 灯泡里的细丝骤然发亮，电流沿铜线一路奔涌
scene: 暴雨整夜拍打窗户，村里一片漆黑，只有诊所的发电机还在响。The storm cut off the electricity to the whole village.
sceneCN: 这里 electricity 是「电力供应」（第 2 个义项：输送到住宅与村镇的电）；句意是这场暴风雨切断了整个村子的供电。

pos.zh: 电；电能；电力供应；电学；紧张兴奋的气氛

senses.title: The energy of moving charges
senses.definition: the energy produced by the movement of electric charges, which can light a lamp or drive a machine
senses.definitionCN: 由电荷运动产生的能量，可以点灯或驱动机器
senses.example: Copper wire carries electricity well.
senses.exampleCN: 铜线导电性能很好。
senses.why: The -ity ending turns the adjective electric into a noun of quality, and that quality is the energy a charged body holds.
senses.whyCN: -ity 词尾把形容词 electric 变成表性质的名词，而带电物体所持有的那种性质就是这股能量。

senses.title: A supply to buildings
senses.definition: the supply of electric power through wires to homes, offices and streets
senses.definitionCN: 通过电线输送到住宅、办公室与街道的电力
senses.example: The storm cut off the electricity to the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 这场暴风雨切断了整个村子的供电。
senses.why: Once the energy is piped into buildings, the abstract force becomes a service that can be billed or cut off.
senses.whyCN: 这股能量一旦被送进建筑，抽象的力量就变成一项能开账单、也能被切断的服务。

senses.title: The science of the force
senses.definition: the branch of physics that studies electric charge, current and their effects
senses.definitionCN: 研究电荷、电流及其效应的物理学分支
senses.example: He is reading a history of electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 他正在读一部电学史。
senses.why: A named force needs a science, and English let the same noun do both jobs instead of coining a separate term.
senses.whyCN: 一股被命名的力需要一门科学，而英语让同一个名词兼做两件事，没有另造新词。

senses.title: A charged atmosphere
senses.definition: a feeling of tense excitement that seems to fill a room or a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 仿佛充满整个房间或人群的紧张兴奋感
senses.example: There was electricity in the air before the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会开始前，空气里满是紧张兴奋的气氛。
senses.why: A charged body makes hair stand up, and a charged room makes people tense, so the physical charge lends its name to excitement.
senses.whyCN: 带电的物体会让汗毛竖起，带电的房间会让人紧绷，于是物理的电荷把名字借给了兴奋感。

intro.en: Electricity is electric plus the Latin noun ending -ity; electric itself goes back through Latin electrum to Greek elektron, amber, whose rubbed surface first showed attraction.
intro.cn: electricity 是 electric 加拉丁语名词词尾 -ity；electric 本身经拉丁语 electrum 上溯到希腊语 elektron（琥珀），琥珀摩擦后的表面最先显现出吸引现象。

items.en: Elektron meant amber, the resin that crackles and attracts when rubbed.
items.cn: elektron 意为「琥珀」，这种树脂摩擦后会噼啪作响并吸引碎屑。

items.en: Latin took the word as electrum, naming both amber and a pale gold-silver alloy.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入作 electrum，既指琥珀，也指一种淡金色的金银合金。

items.en: Seventeenth-century experimenters coined electricus for bodies that attract and repel after rubbing.
items.cn: 十七世纪的实验者造出 electricus，指摩擦后能吸引与排斥的物体。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective and used it for the force as well as the objects.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，既用于物体，也用于那股力。

items.en: Adding -ity produced a noun for the force itself, recorded in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 加上 -ity 造出指这股力本身的名词，十七世纪已有记载。

items.en: The utility sense and the metaphor of a charged room grew out of the same noun.
items.cn: 供电义与「带电房间」的比喻，都是从同一个名词里长出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the electricity family; the near-meaning group separates the energy from power, current and energy itself.
note.cn: 形近组收 electricity 词族；近义组把这份「电」与 power、current、energy 区分开。

entries.definition: Of the force itself, or of one device that runs on it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电的；用电的」，多指力量本身或单个器具。

entries.definition: Of electricity as a system of wiring and engineering.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电气的」，指布线与工程意义上的电。

entries.definition: A tradesperson who installs and repairs wiring.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电工」。

entries.definition: To charge with electricity, or to thrill someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使通电；使震惊」。

entries.definition: The supply of energy to a building, often used for electricity in the home.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电力、动力」，常用来指住宅的供电。

entries.definition: The flow of charge through a wire; a rate, not the energy itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电流」，指电荷在导线中的流动，是速率而非能量本身。

entries.definition: The general capacity to do work, of which electricity is one form.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「能量」，是做功的一般能力，电只是其中一种形式。

entries.definition: The plain word for the feeling that the charged metaphor describes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「兴奋」，是那种带电气氛所比喻的直白说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from amber rubbed in the dark and follow the spark into wires, bills and a tense room.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从黑暗中摩擦的琥珀出发，让火花一路走进电线、电费单与紧绷的房间。

normal.en: Electric plus -ity: the quality of being electric becomes a substance you can bill.
normal.cn: electric 加 -ity：带电的性质变成一种能开账单的东西。

normal.en: Amber rubbed on wool is the first experiment behind the word.
normal.cn: 琥珀在羊毛上摩擦，是这个词背后最早的那个实验。

normal.en: Static electricity clings; current electricity flows.
normal.cn: static electricity 停在原地；current electricity 沿导线流动。

normal.en: Cut off the electricity and the whole village goes dark.
normal.cn: 切断 electricity，整个村子就黑了。

normal.en: A room full of electricity is a room where nobody can sit still.
normal.cn: 满是 electricity 的房间，就是没人坐得住的那个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a copper wire as a river, with charge instead of water.
abstract.cn: 把铜线想成一条河，河里流的不是水，而是电荷。

abstract.en: The same river can be a science, a bill, or a mood.
abstract.cn: 同一条河可以是一门科学、一张账单，也可以是一种情绪。

abstract.en: Electricity is a name for a force that behaves like a fluid and a feeling.
abstract.cn: electricity 是一股力的名字，它既像流体，又像情绪。

examples.en: Copper wire carries electricity well.
examples.cn: 铜线导电性能很好。

examples.en: The storm cut off the electricity to the whole village.
examples.cn: 这场暴风雨切断了整个村子的供电。

examples.en: There was electricity in the air before the concert.
examples.cn: 音乐会开始前，空气里满是紧张兴奋的气氛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一来克锤西提」——按下开关，铜线里那股劲儿立刻冲到灯泡里

root: 由 electric 加拉丁语名词词尾 -ity 构成；electric 源自希腊语 elektron「琥珀」，经拉丁语 electrum 与近代拉丁语 electricus 而来。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of electricity: the energy itself, the supply to buildings, the science that studies it, and the metaphor of a tense room.
sensesIntro.cn: electricity 的四个义项：能量本身、输送到建筑的供电、研究它的学科，以及「紧绷房间」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a filament flaring inside a bulb as current races along a copper wire.
core.cn: 核心意象：电流沿铜线奔涌，灯泡里的细丝骤然发亮。

branches.en: THE ENERGY: charge in motion, measured and used.
branches.cn: 能量线：运动中的电荷，被计量、被使用。

branches.en: THE SUPPLY: the same energy delivered as a service.
branches.cn: 供给线：同一股能量以服务的形式送到门口。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE: the force turned into an object of study.
branches.cn: 学科线：这股力变成被研究的对象。

branches.en: THE FEELING: a charged room borrows the physical word.
branches.cn: 情绪线：带电的房间借用了这个物理词。

branches.en: THE CURRENT: what flows in the wire is what arrives at the socket.
branches.cn: 电流线：导线里流动的东西，正是插座里到达的东西。

intro.en: Electricity is electric plus the Latin noun ending -ity; the stem behind it is the Greek word for amber.
intro.cn: electricity 是 electric 加拉丁语名词词尾 -ity；它背后的词干是希腊语里表示「琥珀」的词。

latinIntro.en: Greek elektron and Latin electrum are recorded; electricus and electricity were coined later by scientists.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 elektron 与拉丁语 electrum 有记录；electricus 与 electricity 是后来由科学家造出的。

items.example: It carried the word into Latin.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个词带入拉丁语。

items.example: It was coined in the seventeenth century.
It is the base of the whole family.

definition_zh: 电子；（作定语）电子的；价电子
definition_en: a very small particle with a negative charge that moves around the nucleus of an atom
core_image: 原子中心一颗核，外面几个极小的光点绕着它飞
scene: 示波管里一束细线被磁场轻轻推开，屏幕上留下弯曲的轨迹。A beam of electrons bends as it passes the magnet.
sceneCN: 这里 electron 是「电子」（第 1 个义项：带负电的亚原子粒子）；句意是一束电子经过磁铁时发生了偏转。

pos.zh: 电子；价电子；（作定语）电子的

senses.title: The negative particle
senses.definition: a stable subatomic particle with a negative charge that orbits the nucleus of an atom
senses.definitionCN: 一种带负电、绕原子核运动的稳定亚原子粒子
senses.example: An electron carries a negative charge.
senses.exampleCN: 一个电子带负电荷。
senses.why: When physicists needed a name for the tiny carrier of charge, they reached back to the amber root that had named the force.
senses.whyCN: 物理学家要给电荷的微小载体命名时，又回到了当初为这股力命名的「琥珀」词根。

senses.title: Before a noun as a tool
senses.definition: used before another noun for devices or beams that steer electrons, as in electron microscope
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，指操控电子束的装置，如电子显微镜
senses.example: The lab bought a new electron microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室买了一台新的电子显微镜。
senses.why: The particle became a measuring tool, so its name moved in front of the instrument it drives.
senses.whyCN: 这个粒子成了测量工具，于是它的名字挪到了由它驱动的仪器前面。

senses.title: The electron in a bond
senses.definition: an outer electron that an atom shares or trades when it forms a chemical bond
senses.definitionCN: 原子成键时交出或共享的外层电子
senses.example: Each carbon atom shares four electrons.
senses.exampleCN: 每个碳原子共享四个电子。
senses.why: Chemistry counts only the outermost electrons when it explains bonds, and each one keeps the same name.
senses.whyCN: 化学在解释成键时只数最外层电子，而每一个仍用同一个名字。

intro.en: Electron revives a Greek word for amber; the modern particle name was proposed at the end of the nineteenth century and confirmed when the particle itself was found.
intro.cn: electron 复活了希腊语里表示「琥珀」的词；这个现代粒子名在十九世纪末被提出，并在粒子本身被发现后得到确认。

items.en: Elektron meant amber, and later also the pale alloy that looked like it.
items.cn: elektron 意为「琥珀」，后来也指外观相似的淡色合金。

items.en: Latin kept the word as electrum and passed the root into the science of charge.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留作 electrum，并把这个词根传进了研究电荷的科学。

items.en: The adjective electric made the root familiar before the particle had a name.
items.cn: 在粒子得名之前，形容词 electric 已让这个词根为人熟悉。

items.en: The physicist Stoney proposed electron as the name of a unit of charge.
items.cn: 物理学家斯通尼提议用 electron 作为电荷单位的名称。

items.en: Thomson's experiments showed that a real particle carried that charge.
items.cn: 汤姆孙的实验证明真的有一种粒子携带这份电荷。

items.en: The name settled on the particle, and the suffix -ic later produced electronic.
items.cn: 这个名字最终固定给了粒子，而 -ic 词尾后来造出了 electronic。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the electric family; the near-meaning group sorts the atom's particles and the charge they carry.
note.cn: 形近组收 electric 词族；近义组区分原子里的几种粒子以及它们携带的电荷。

entries.definition: Of the force, or of a device driven by it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电的；用电的」。

entries.definition: Working by controlling electrons in circuits.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电子的」，靠控制电路中的电子工作。

entries.definition: The science of electron control, or the circuits themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电子学；电子器件」。

entries.definition: The energy of moving charges.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电；电力」。

entries.definition: A particle in the nucleus with a positive charge; equal and opposite to the electron.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「质子」，位于核内、带正电，与电子电量相等、符号相反。

entries.definition: A particle in the nucleus with no charge at all.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「中子」，位于核内，不带电。

entries.definition: An atom that has gained or lost electrons and so carries a charge.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「离子」，是得失电子后带电的原子。

entries.definition: The property itself that the electron carries, not the particle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电荷」，是电子所携带的性质，而不是粒子本身。

normalIntro.en: These hooks shrink the amber word down to a point of charge and then hand it to microscopes and bonds.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把「琥珀」那个词缩小成一个电荷点，再交给显微镜与化学键。

normal.en: Electron is the smallest piece of the amber story.
normal.cn: electron 是琥珀这个故事里最小的一块。

normal.en: Protons sit in the middle; electrons run around them.
normal.cn: 质子坐在正中，电子绕着它们跑。

normal.en: An electron microscope sees with particles, not with light.
normal.cn: 电子显微镜用粒子看东西，而不是用光。

normal.en: Bonds are electron deals: share one, give one away.
normal.cn: 化学键就是电子的交易：共享一个，或送走一个。

normal.en: Electric is the field; electron is the smallest worker in it.
normal.cn: electric 是整片场；electron 是场里最小的那个工人。

abstract.en: Picture a nucleus as a lit lamp and electrons as moths circling it.
abstract.cn: 把原子核想成一盏亮着的灯，电子就是绕着它飞的蛾子。

abstract.en: The same word names one particle and a whole technology built on it.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既命名一种粒子，也命名建立在它之上的整套技术。

abstract.en: Electron is a point of charge; everything electronic is that point multiplied.
abstract.cn: electron 是一个电荷点；一切 electronic 的东西都是这个点的千百倍复制。

examples.en: An electron carries a negative charge.
examples.cn: 一个电子带负电荷。

examples.en: A beam of electrons bends as it passes the magnet.
examples.cn: 一束电子经过磁铁时发生了偏转。

examples.en: Each carbon atom shares four electrons.
examples.cn: 每个碳原子共享四个电子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一颗来克胀」——原子外那颗极小的光点，绕一圈又一圈

root: 源自希腊语 elektron「琥珀」，经拉丁语 electrum 进入英语的科学词汇；十九世纪末被用来命名带负电的粒子。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of electron: the particle, the word used before an instrument's name, and the outer electron counted in bonds.
sensesIntro.cn: electron 的三个义项：粒子本身、放在仪器名前作定语，以及成键时被计数的外层电子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small bright point circling a heavy nucleus.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个明亮的小点绕着重核旋转。

branches.en: THE PARTICLE: the carrier of negative charge.
branches.cn: 粒子线：负电荷的载体。

branches.en: THE TOOL: the same name in front of an instrument.
branches.cn: 工具线：同一个名字被放在仪器前面。

branches.en: THE BOND: the outer electron that chemistry counts.
branches.cn: 成键线：化学所数的外层电子。

branches.en: THE OUTERMOST: the electron that is shared is still the same particle.
branches.cn: 最外层线：被共享的那个电子仍然是同一种粒子。

branches.en: THE BEAM: many electrons lined up become an instrument.
branches.cn: 电子束线：许多电子排齐，就成了一件仪器。

intro.en: Electron is built on the amber root plus the Greek noun ending -on; the same root feeds electric and electronic.
intro.cn: electron 用「琥珀」词根加希腊语名词词尾 -on 构成；同一个词根还养出 electric 与 electronic。

latinIntro.en: Greek elektron and Latin electrum are the recorded forms; electron as a particle name is modern.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 elektron 与拉丁语 electrum 是有记录的形式；作为粒子名的 electron 属于现代造词。

items.example: It names the substance that started it all.
items.exampleCN: 它命名了这一切的起点物质。

items.example: It passed the root on to Latin.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个词根传给拉丁语。
它让这个词根为人熟悉。
它命名一种亚原子粒子。

items.example: It appears in electron and proton.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 electron 与 proton 中。

definition_zh: 电子的；电子设备的；电子化的；电子音乐的；电子学的
definition_en: working by controlling the flow of electrons in circuits, using computer or network technology, made with synthesizers, or relating to the science of electronics
core_image: 电路板上密布芯片与细如发丝的走线，指示灯一闪一闪
scene: 超市收银台前，顾客把手机贴在读卡器上，滴一声就完成了付款。Most shops now accept electronic payment.
sceneCN: 这里 electronic 是「电子化的、用电子手段完成的」（第 2 个义项：借助计算机与网络技术）；句意是多数商店现在都接受电子支付。

pos.zh: 电子的；电子设备的；电子化的；电子音乐的；电子学的

senses.title: Working through circuits
senses.titleCN: 电子的；靠电子电路工作的
senses.definition: operating by controlling the movement of electrons through circuits such as transistors and chips
senses.definitionCN: 通过控制电子在晶体管、芯片等电路中流动来工作
senses.example: The lab is testing a new electronic circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室正在测试一块新的电子电路。
senses.why: The suffix -ic turns the particle name into an adjective, so the word describes anything that works by steering electrons.
senses.whyCN: -ic 词尾把粒子名变成形容词，于是这个词形容一切靠操控电子来工作的东西。

senses.title: Done by computer or network
senses.titleCN: 电子化的；用电子手段完成的
senses.definition: carried out using computers, networks or digital systems rather than paper or face-to-face contact
senses.definitionCN: 借助计算机、网络或数字系统完成，而不是纸面或面对面
senses.example: Most shops now accept electronic payment.
senses.exampleCN: 多数商店现在都接受电子支付。
senses.why: Once a whole transaction runs through chips and networks, the device adjective spreads to the activity itself.
senses.whyCN: 当一笔交易整个跑在芯片与网络上，指设备的形容词就扩展到了活动本身。

senses.title: Made with synthesizers
senses.definition: of music produced with synthesizers, samplers and other electronic instruments
senses.definitionCN: 用合成器、采样器及其他电子乐器制作的音乐
senses.example: She writes electronic music on a laptop.
senses.exampleCN: 她在笔记本电脑上写电子音乐。
senses.why: The instruments are the style, so the adjective naming the technology ended up naming a whole genre.
senses.whyCN: 乐器就是风格本身，于是命名这项技术的形容词最后成了一个音乐流派的名称。

senses.title: Of the science of electronics
senses.definition: relating to electronics as a branch of engineering and physics
senses.definitionCN: 指作为工程学与物理学分支的电子学
senses.example: He teaches electronic engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 他教电子工程。
senses.why: The field that studies these circuits needed a name, and the adjective before engineering supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 研究这些电路的那门学科需要名字，而 engineering 前面的这个形容词正好提供了它。

intro.en: Electronic is electron plus -ic, coined once the particle had been found; the root itself is the Greek word for amber.
intro.cn: electronic 是 electron 加 -ic，在粒子被发现之后才造出；而这个词根本身是希腊语里的「琥珀」。

items.en: Elektron named amber, whose rubbed surface first showed attraction.
items.cn: elektron 指琥珀，摩擦后的表面最先显现出吸引现象。

items.en: Latin kept electrum for amber and passed the root into modern science.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留 electrum 表示琥珀，并把这个词根传进近代科学。

items.en: The particle name electron gave the family a solid centre.
items.cn: 粒子名 electron 为这个词族提供了坚实的中心。

items.en: Valves and then transistors made a new adjective necessary for circuits.
items.cn: 电子管以及后来的晶体管，使指电路的形容词成为必需。

items.en: The -ic form covered devices, then transactions, then music.
items.cn: 加 -ic 的形式先指设备，再指交易，最后指音乐。

items.en: Electronic now names a whole layer of daily life built on chips.
items.cn: 如今 electronic 命名了建立在芯片之上的整整一层日常生活。

note.en: The look-alike group lines up the electric family; the near-meaning group separates electronic from electric, digital and electrical.
note.cn: 形近组排开 electric 词族；近义组区分 electronic 与 electric、digital、electrical。

entries.definition: The negative particle that these circuits control.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电子」，正是这些电路所控制的粒子。

entries.definition: The science of such circuits, or the circuits as goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电子学」，也指作为商品的电子器件。

entries.definition: By electronic means.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「用电子方式地」。

entries.definition: Of wiring and power systems rather than of chips.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电气的」，指布线供电系统而非芯片。

entries.definition: Driven by electricity in the plain sense, as a kettle or a motor.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「用电的」，指水壶、马达这类普通用电的东西。

entries.definition: Stored as numbers; overlaps the network sense but says nothing about circuits.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「数字的」，与网络义重叠，但不涉及电路。

entries.definition: Belonging to the power system, a wider and older field.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电气的」，属于更宽、更早的电力领域。

entries.definition: Run by machines; close to the transaction sense but not tied to chips.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「自动化的」，接近交易义，但不限于芯片。

normalIntro.en: These hooks walk from a single electron to a chip, then to a payment, a track and a degree.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一个电子走到一块芯片，再走到一笔支付、一首曲子与一个学位。

normal.en: One electron is a particle; electronic is a whole way of working.
normal.cn: 一个电子是粒子；electronic 则是一整套工作方式。

normal.en: Electric kettles heat; electronic devices decide.
normal.cn: electric 水壶负责加热；electronic 设备负责判断。

normal.en: Electronic mail is mail without paper.
normal.cn: electronic mail 就是没有纸的邮件。

normal.en: Electronic music is music without a visible instrument.
normal.cn: electronic music 就是看不见乐器的音乐。

normal.en: A chip is a city of electrons with traffic rules.
normal.cn: 一块芯片就是一座有交通规则的电子之城。

abstract.en: Picture a circuit board as an aerial map of a small city at night.
abstract.cn: 把电路板想成夜里一座小城市的航拍图。

abstract.en: Electrons are the traffic; the chip is the road plan.
abstract.cn: 电子是车流；芯片是道路规划。

abstract.en: Electronic is what happens when the smallest particle is put in charge of the biggest systems.
abstract.cn: electronic 就是最小的粒子掌管最大系统时发生的事。

examples.en: The lab is testing a new electronic circuit.
examples.cn: 实验室正在测试一块新的电子电路。

examples.en: Most shops now accept electronic payment.
examples.cn: 多数商店现在都接受电子支付。

examples.en: She writes electronic music on a laptop.
examples.cn: 她在笔记本电脑上写电子音乐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一颗来克胀尼克」——芯片上密密麻麻的走线一起闪，机器就活了

root: 由 electron 加形容词词尾 -ic 构成；electron 源自希腊语 elektron「琥珀」，经拉丁语 electrum 进入英语科学词汇。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of electronic: circuits, computer-based activities, synth music, and the engineering field.
sensesIntro.cn: electronic 的四个义项：电子电路、依托计算机的活动、合成器音乐，以及电子工程学科。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chip with hair-thin tracks and a blinking indicator light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块芯片，走线细如发丝，指示灯一闪一闪。

branches.en: THE CIRCUIT: electrons steered by transistors and chips.
branches.cn: 电路线：由晶体管与芯片操控的电子。

branches.en: THE TRANSACTION: money and mail moved through networks.
branches.cn: 交易线：透过网络转移的钱与邮件。

branches.en: THE GENRE: a style named after its instruments.
branches.cn: 流派线：以乐器命名的一种音乐风格。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the engineering that designs the circuits.
branches.cn: 学科线：设计这些电路的工程学。

branches.en: THE CHIP: every paperless payment is a chip doing arithmetic.
branches.cn: 芯片线：每一笔无纸支付，都是芯片在做算术。

intro.en: Electronic is electron with the adjective suffix -ic; the root behind both is the Greek word for amber.
intro.cn: electronic 是 electron 加形容词词尾 -ic；两者背后的词根都是希腊语的「琥珀」。

latinIntro.en: Greek elektron and Latin electrum are the older recorded forms; electron and electronic are modern coinages.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 elektron 与拉丁语 electrum 是较早的有记录形式；electron 与 electronic 都是现代造词。

items.example: It is the root of the whole family.
It supplies the stem of this word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了这个词的词干。

definition_zh: 优雅的；高雅的；雅致的；简洁精妙的
definition_en: graceful and stylish in appearance or manner, pleasingly simple in design, or neat and clever as a solution
core_image: 一个人穿着剪裁利落的深色长裙，走过大厅时几乎不发出声音
scene: 评审会上，年轻工程师在白板上写下三行公式，难题当场解开。Her elegant proof took only three lines.
sceneCN: 这里 elegant 是「（方案）简洁精妙的」（第 3 个义项：以最少的步骤漂亮地解决问题）；句意是她的证明只用了三行。

pos.zh: 优雅的；高雅的；雅致的；简洁精妙的

senses.title: Graceful in manner
senses.definition: moving, speaking or behaving with natural grace and good taste
senses.definitionCN: 举止、言谈自然而得体，显出良好的品味
senses.example: She gave an elegant bow at the end of the performance.
senses.exampleCN: 演出结束时，她优雅地鞠了一躬。
senses.why: Latin elegans first meant choosy and tasteful, and a person who chooses well in movement looks graceful.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 elegans 最初意为「挑剔的、有品味的」，而在举止上选得恰到好处的人，看上去就优雅。

senses.title: Stylish and simple in design
senses.definition: pleasingly simple and well proportioned, without anything extra
senses.definitionCN: 简洁而比例匀称，没有任何多余之物
senses.example: The room was simple but elegant.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间简单却很雅致。
senses.why: Good taste removes rather than adds, so the same word praises a design for what it leaves out.
senses.whyCN: 好品味是删而不是加，于是同一个词用「省掉了什么」来称赞一件设计。

senses.title: Neat and clever as a solution
senses.definition: of a proof, method or solution, achieved in few steps with surprising neatness
senses.definitionCN: 指证明、方法或方案步骤极少却出人意料地漂亮
senses.example: Her elegant proof took only three lines.
senses.exampleCN: 她的证明只用了三行。
senses.why: A proof that wastes nothing is admired the way a graceful body is, so the aesthetic word moved into mathematics.
senses.whyCN: 一条不浪费任何步骤的证明，会被像欣赏优雅身姿那样欣赏，于是这个审美词走进了数学。

intro.en: Elegant comes from Latin elegans, a word for tasteful and choosy, built on eligere, to pick out; it reached English through French.
intro.cn: elegant 来自拉丁语 elegans，意为「有品味的、会挑选的」，其根是 eligere（挑出）；它经法语进入英语。

items.en: Eligere meant to pick out or choose, from ex plus legere, to gather.
items.cn: eligere 意为「挑出、选择」，由 ex 加 legere（收取）构成。

items.en: The participle elegans described someone who chooses well and so has fine taste.
items.cn: 分词 elegans 形容一个人会挑选，因而品味出众。

items.en: French borrowed the word for refined and handsome.
items.cn: 法语借入这个词，表示「精致的、俊雅的」。

items.en: English took it for manners and dress that show good taste.
items.cn: 英语借入它，指表现出好品味的举止与衣着。

items.en: Design and mathematics extended it to anything done with the fewest parts.
items.cn: 设计与数学把它扩展到一切「用最少部件完成」的事物上。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps elegance and its false friend elegy apart; the near-meaning group sorts grace, style and refinement.
note.cn: 形近组把 elegance 与易混的 elegy 分开；近义组区分 grace、style 与 refinement。

entries.definition: The quality of being elegant; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「优雅；雅致；简洁」，是本词的派生名词。

entries.definition: In an elegant manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「优雅地；简洁地」。

entries.definition: Lacking grace or taste; the in- prefix reverses the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不雅的；笨拙的」，由 in- 否定本词。

entries.definition: A mournful poem; it looks close but has a different root and means sorrow.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「挽歌」，形近但词源不同，意思是哀悼。

entries.definition: Smooth and flowing in movement; about the body rather than taste.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「优美的」，强调动作流畅，而非品味。

entries.definition: Fashionable and striking; more about current trend than restraint.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「时髦的」，更看重当下潮流而非克制。

entries.definition: Polished by culture and training; the result of long cultivation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有修养的、精炼的」，是长期教养的结果。

entries.definition: Neat and well dressed, or clever; broader and more casual.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「整洁漂亮的；聪明的」，更宽泛也更口语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to choosing well, then let that taste spread from a person to a room to a proof.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把词义系在「会挑」上，再让这份品味从人扩到房间、再到一条证明。

normal.en: Elegant and elect share the Latin verb to choose.
normal.cn: elegant 与 elect 共用一个拉丁语动词，意思是「挑选」。

normal.en: Good taste is mostly what you leave out.
normal.cn: 好品味多半在于你省掉了什么。

normal.en: An elegant dress has no extra line on it.
normal.cn: 一件 elegant 的连衣裙，身上没有多余的一道线。

normal.en: An elegant proof has no extra step in it.
normal.cn: 一条 elegant 的证明，里面没有多余的一步。

normal.en: Elegy is a funeral song; elegant is good taste. Keep them apart.
normal.cn: elegy 是挽歌，elegant 是好品味，别把两者混在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a hand picking one fruit from a full basket, without hesitating.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从满篮水果里毫不犹豫地挑出一只。

abstract.en: Choice made clean is what the eye calls beautiful.
abstract.cn: 干净利落的选择，眼睛就称之为美。

abstract.en: Elegant is the shape of a decision that needed nothing more.
abstract.cn: elegant 是一个「再不需要多一点」的决定所呈现的形状。

examples.en: She gave an elegant bow at the end of the performance.
examples.cn: 演出结束时，她优雅地鞠了一躬。

examples.en: The room was simple but elegant.
examples.cn: 这个房间简单却很雅致。

examples.en: Her elegant proof took only three lines.
examples.cn: 她的证明只用了三行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艾勒甘」——挑衣服只挑一件，穿上就再不用添任何配饰

root: 源自拉丁语 elegans「有品味的、会挑选的」，其根为 eligere（挑出，由 ex + legere 构成），经法语 élégant 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of elegant: graceful bearing, tasteful simplicity in design, and neatness in a proof or solution.
sensesIntro.cn: elegant 的三个义项：优雅的举止、设计上的雅致简洁，以及证明或方案上的简洁精妙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand choosing one perfect fruit from a full basket.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从满篮水果中挑出一只最合适的。

branches.en: THE BEARING: a person whose movements show good choice.
branches.cn: 举止线：动作里显出好眼光的人。

branches.en: THE DESIGN: simplicity praised as good taste.
branches.cn: 设计线：被当作好品味来称赞的简洁。

branches.en: THE PROOF: the same restraint applied to reasoning.
branches.cn: 证明线：同样的克制用在推理上。

branches.en: THE SPARE: what is left out is the compliment.
branches.cn: 删减线：省掉的部分才是称赞所在。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: a graceful body and a graceful room are read the same way.
branches.cn: 外观线：优雅的身姿与雅致的房间，读法完全相同。

intro.en: Elegant is the Latin participle elegans, from eligere, to pick out; the -ant ending is the mark of that participle.
intro.cn: elegant 就是拉丁语分词 elegans，出自 eligere（挑出）；-ant 词尾正是这个分词的标记。

latinIntro.en: Eligere and elegans are recorded Latin forms; English took the word through French rather than directly.
latinIntro.cn: eligere 与 elegans 都是有记录的拉丁语形式；英语是经法语而非直接借入这个词的。

items.example: It supplies the root of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了这个词的词根。

items.example: It is the parent of elegans.

items.meaningCN: 处于某种状态或正在做

definition_zh: 元素；（构成整体的）要素；成分；少量；[the elements] 恶劣天气
definition_en: a simple chemical substance that cannot be split by chemical means, one part of a whole, a small amount of a quality, or the forces of weather
core_image: 摊开的元素周期表，一格一格印着字母符号
scene: 老师在黑板上画了一张周期表，一格一格写着字母和数字，指尖停在碳那一格。Carbon is an element found in every living thing.
sceneCN: 这里 element 是「化学元素」（第 1 个义项：由同种原子构成、不能用化学方法再分的物质）；句意是碳是每个生物体内都能找到的元素。

pos.zh: 元素；要素；成分；少量；[复数] 恶劣天气

derivatives.zh: 基本的；自然力的；元素的

senses.title: A chemical element
senses.definition: a substance made of only one kind of atom, which cannot be broken down by chemical means
senses.definitionCN: 只由一种原子构成的物质，无法用化学方法再分
senses.example: Oxygen is the most common element in the earth's crust.
senses.exampleCN: 氧是地壳中含量最多的元素。
senses.why: Elementum first named a first principle, a unit you cannot go behind; chemistry kept exactly that role for the simplest substances.
senses.whyCN: elementum 最初指「不可再往前拆的第一原则」，化学把完全相同的角色留给了最简单的物质。

senses.title: A part of a whole
senses.definition: one of the parts or qualities that together make up a whole thing
senses.definitionCN: 共同构成某一整体的部分或性质之一
senses.example: Trust is a key element of any friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 信任是任何友谊的关键要素。
senses.why: If an element is an irreducible unit, then a complex thing is merely a set of such units, so the word names any necessary part.
senses.whyCN: 既然 element 是不可再分的单位，复杂事物就只是一组这样的单位，于是这个词指任何必要的组成部分。

senses.title: A small amount of a quality
senses.definition: a small but noticeable amount of a quality or feeling within something larger
senses.definitionCN: 某个较大事物中少量却可察觉的性质或情绪
senses.example: There is an element of truth in what she says.
senses.exampleCN: 她说的话里有几分道理。
senses.why: The irreducible unit can be tiny, so an element became a small measure of something mixed in.
senses.whyCN: 不可再分的单位可以很小，于是 element 变成掺在其中的一点分量。

senses.title: Wind rain and cold
senses.definition: the forces of weather, especially bad weather, used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 天气的力量，尤指恶劣天气，多用复数
senses.example: The tent kept out the elements.
senses.exampleCN: 这顶帐篷挡住了风吹雨打。
senses.why: The old four elements were earth, air, fire and water, and the open sky was thought to be their arena, so weather became the elements.
senses.whyCN: 古老的四元素是土、气、火、水，而开阔的天空被当作它们的战场，于是天气就成了 the elements。

intro.en: Element comes from Latin elementum, a word of debated origin meaning a first principle; note that the opening e- is part of the stem, not a prefix.
intro.cn: element 来自拉丁语 elementum，意为「第一原则」，其来源至今有争议；注意开头的 e- 属于词干本身，不是前缀。

items.en: Elementum named a first principle and also the letters of the alphabet, the units of writing.
items.cn: elementum 指第一原则，也指字母表里的字母，即书写的单位。

items.en: In the plural it named the four basic substances: earth, water, air and fire.
items.cn: 复数形式指四种基本物质：土、水、气、火。

items.en: French kept the word for a basic component of anything.
items.cn: 法语保留这个词，指任何事物的基本组成部分。

items.en: English used it for the four substances and for the parts of a whole.
items.cn: 英语用它指四种元素，也指整体的各个部分。

items.en: With modern chemistry the word was fixed to substances defined by atomic number.
items.cn: 随着近代化学的发展，这个词被固定给按原子序数定义的物质。

items.en: The weather sense survives in the plural, the quality sense in phrases like an element of truth.
items.cn: 天气义留在复数中，性质义留在 an element of truth 这类短语里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the element family; the near-meaning group separates a component, an ingredient, a factor and a substance.
note.cn: 形近组收 element 词族；近义组区分 component、ingredient、factor 与 substance。

entries.definition: Of the elements or of raw natural forces; basic and powerful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「基本的；自然力的」，带原始力量感。

entries.definition: At the simplest level; also the adjective for basic particles.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「基础的；初级的」，也用于基本粒子。

entries.definition: matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid
entries.definitionCN: 沉积物；沉淀

entries.definition: A part of a machine or system; more technical than element.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部件、组件」，比 element 更技术化。

entries.definition: One of the things mixed into a recipe or a product.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成分、配料」，指混进配方或产品里的东西。

entries.definition: One thing that influences a result; about causes rather than parts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「因素」，指影响结果的原因，而非组成的部分。

entries.definition: A material with a definite make-up; the physical side of the chemical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「物质」，是元素义在物理层面的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the word close to its Latin sense of a unit you cannot break, then spread that unit across chemistry, wholes and weather.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子让词义贴近拉丁语「拆不开的单位」，再把单位铺到化学、整体与天气上。

normal.en: The e- in element is not a prefix; elementum is one solid stem.
normal.cn: element 开头的 e- 不是前缀，elementum 整个是实心词干。

normal.en: A chemical element is the last stop: split it and it is no longer that element.
normal.cn: 化学 element 是终点：再分下去，它就不是那个元素了。

normal.en: An element of a plan is one brick that cannot be left out.
normal.cn: 计划里的一个 element，就是一块不能少的砖。

normal.en: An element of truth is a small piece that cannot be split further.
normal.cn: an element of truth 就是一粒再拆不开的真话。

normal.en: The weather outside is the elements because the sky was their arena.
normal.cn: 外面的天气叫 the elements，因为天空曾是四元素的战场。

abstract.en: Picture a table where every cell holds one letter and one number.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表格，每一格只装一个字母和一个数字。

abstract.en: Everything complicated is a stack of these single cells.
abstract.cn: 一切复杂的东西，都是这些单格堆起来的。

abstract.en: Element is the smallest block that still keeps its own name.
abstract.cn: element 是仍然保有自己名字的最小一块。

examples.en: Oxygen is the most common element in the earth's crust.
examples.cn: 氧是地壳中含量最多的元素。

examples.en: Trust is a key element of any friendship.
examples.cn: 信任是任何友谊的关键要素。

examples.en: There is an element of truth in what she says.
examples.cn: 她说的话里有几分道理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艾勒门特」——元素周期表一格一格，每格只住一个住户

root: 源自拉丁语 elementum「第一原则；字母」，来源有争议；开头的 e- 不是前缀，而是词干的一部分，与 elevate 的 e-（＝ex-）不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of element: the chemical substance, a necessary part, a small amount of a quality, and the weather in the plural.
sensesIntro.cn: element 的四个义项：化学元素、必要组成部分、少量的某种性质，以及复数形式的恶劣天气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a periodic table whose cells each hold one letter and one number.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张周期表，每格只装一个字母和一个数字。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: one kind of atom, named by number.
branches.cn: 物质线：一种原子，以序数命名。

branches.en: THE PART: a unit that a whole cannot do without.
branches.cn: 部分线：整体少不了的那个单位。

branches.en: THE TRACE: the same unit shrunk to a hint.
branches.cn: 微量线：同一个单位缩小成一缕线索。

branches.en: THE WEATHER: the old four elements turned into sky.
branches.cn: 天气线：古老的四元素化作头顶的天空。

branches.en: THE TABLE: chemistry and plain parts share one word.
branches.cn: 表格线：化学与日常的「部分」共用一个词。

intro.en: Element has no prefix: the whole word is the Latin stem elementum, and the -ment at the end is a worn-down ending rather than the English suffix.
intro.cn: element 没有前缀：整个词就是拉丁词干 elementum，末尾的 -ment 是磨损后的词尾，不是英语后缀 -ment。

latinIntro.en: Elementum and its plural elementa are recorded Latin forms; the word's deeper origin is still disputed.
latinIntro.cn: elementum 及其复数 elementa 是有记录的拉丁语形式；这个词更深的来源至今仍有争议。

items.example: It is the whole stem of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它就是这个词的整个词干。

items.example: It is borrowed with little change.
items.exampleCN: 它几乎未经改动被借入。

items.meaningCN: 磨损的拉丁词尾，并非后缀
items.example: It is not the -ment of movement.
items.exampleCN: 它不是 movement 里的那个 -ment。

derivatives.zh: 基本的；自然力的；元素的

definition_zh: 基础的；初级的；基本的；简单的；（科学）基本粒子的
definition_en: at the simplest and most basic level, dealing with first principles, or relating to the simplest particles of matter
core_image: 一年级教室的黑板上，写着 A B C 三个大写字母
scene: 乡村小学的教室里，孩子们跟着老师一遍遍念字母表。She teaches at a small elementary school.
sceneCN: 这里 elementary 是「初级的、基础的」（第 1 个义项：指教育的最初阶段）；句意是她在一所规模不大的小学教书。

pos.zh: 基础的；初级的；基本的；简单的；基本粒子的

senses.title: At the first stage of school
senses.definition: relating to the first and simplest stage of education or training
senses.definitionCN: 指教育或训练的最初、最简单的阶段
senses.example: She teaches at a small elementary school.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一所规模不大的小学教书。
senses.why: The Latin -ary ending means belonging to, so elementary describes what belongs to the elements, the first things taught.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 -ary 词尾意为「属于」，所以 elementary 形容属于「元素」即最初所学之物的东西。

senses.title: Simple and easy to grasp
senses.definition: so basic that it needs no special knowledge, sometimes used to scold a careless error
senses.definitionCN: 基础到不需要专门知识，有时用来责备粗心的错误
senses.example: He made an elementary mistake in the first line.
senses.exampleCN: 他在第一行就犯了一个低级错误。
senses.why: What belongs to the elements is what every beginner already knows, so the word drifts towards simple and even too simple.
senses.whyCN: 属于「元素」的东西是每个初学者都已知道的，于是这个词滑向「简单」，甚至「简单得不该错」。

senses.title: Of the simplest particles
senses.definition: in physics, describing particles that are not known to be made of smaller parts
senses.definitionCN: 在物理学中形容尚未发现由更小部分构成的粒子
senses.example: Electrons are elementary particles.
senses.exampleCN: 电子是基本粒子。
senses.why: Physics returned the word to its oldest meaning: the unit you cannot split further.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把这个词送回了它最古老的含义：再拆不开的那个单位。

intro.en: Elementary is element plus the Latin adjective ending -ary; there is no e- prefix at all, and the word simply means belonging to the elements.
intro.cn: elementary 是 element 加拉丁语形容词词尾 -ary；它根本没有 e- 前缀，整个词的意思就是「属于元素的」。

items.en: Elementum named a first principle, the smallest thing you can teach or split.
items.cn: elementum 指第一原则，即你能教授或拆分的最小之物。

items.en: The ending -arius formed adjectives meaning belonging to, so elementarius meant of the elements.
items.cn: 词尾 -arius 构成「属于……」的形容词，elementarius 意为「属于元素的」。

items.en: French kept the adjective for what concerns first principles.
items.cn: 法语保留这个形容词，指涉及第一原则的事物。

items.en: English used it for basic teaching and for simple facts.
items.cn: 英语用它指基础教学与简单事实。

items.en: Schools, careless mistakes and physics particles all settled under the same adjective.
items.cn: 学校、粗心错误与物理粒子最后都归在同一个形容词下。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the element family straight; the near-meaning group separates basic, primary, fundamental and simple.
note.cn: 形近组理清 element 词族；近义组区分 basic、primary、fundamental 与 simple。

entries.definition: The noun this adjective is built on.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「元素；要素」，是本词的基干。

entries.definition: Of raw natural forces, with a stronger and older feel than elementary.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「自然力的；基本的」，比 elementary 更有原始力量感。

entries.definition: The adverb, rarely used outside technical prose.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「基础地」，多用于技术性文字。

entries.definition: Forming the base; the most common everyday word for this idea.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「基本的」，是这一概念最日常的说法。

entries.definition: First in order or importance; also used for the first years of school.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「初级的；首要的」，也用于小学阶段。

entries.definition: Serving as a foundation; heavier and more abstract than elementary.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「根本的」，比 elementary 更重、更抽象。

entries.definition: Not complicated; about difficulty, not about stages or particles.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「简单的」，说的是难度，而非阶段或粒子。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word straight from element plus -ary and then walk it from the first school year to the smallest particle.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把词直接拆成 element 加 -ary，再让它从小学一年级一路走到最小的粒子。

normal.en: No e- prefix here: element plus -ary, that is all.
normal.cn: 这里没有 e- 前缀：就是 element 加 -ary，仅此而已。

normal.en: Elementary school teaches the elements of reading and counting.
normal.cn: elementary school 教的就是读书与数数的「元素」。

normal.en: An elementary mistake is one a beginner should already avoid.
normal.cn: an elementary mistake 是初学者本就该避免的错。

normal.en: An elementary particle has nothing smaller inside it yet.
normal.cn: an elementary particle 里面至今找不到更小的东西。

normal.en: Same root as element, but the -ary makes it an adjective.
normal.cn: 与 element 同根，-ary 把它变成形容词。

abstract.en: Picture the first page of a textbook, all letters and dots.
abstract.cn: 想象课本的第一页，全是字母和圆点。

abstract.en: Whatever belongs to that first page is elementary.
abstract.cn: 凡是属于那一页的东西，都是 elementary。

abstract.en: Elementary is where a subject begins, and where physics ends its search.
abstract.cn: elementary 是一门学科开始的地方，也是物理停止追问的地方。

examples.en: She teaches at a small elementary school.
examples.cn: 她在一所规模不大的小学教书。

examples.en: He made an elementary mistake in the first line.
examples.cn: 他在第一行就犯了一个低级错误。

examples.en: Electrons are elementary particles.
examples.cn: 电子是基本粒子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艾勒门特瑞」——小学黑板上那三个大写字母，就是一切的起点

root: 由 element 加拉丁语形容词词尾 -ary 构成，意为「属于元素的」；element 源自拉丁语 elementum，本词不含 e- 前缀。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of elementary: the first stage of schooling, what is too simple to get wrong, and the unsplittable particle.
sensesIntro.cn: elementary 的三个义项：教育的最初阶段、简单到不该出错的层次，以及不可再分的粒子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first page of a textbook, holding only letters and dots.
core.cn: 核心意象：课本第一页，上面只有字母和圆点。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: the first stage, taught from the elements.
branches.cn: 学校线：从「元素」教起的最初阶段。

branches.en: THE SIMPLE: basic enough that an error looks careless.
branches.cn: 简单线：基础到出错就显得粗心。

branches.en: THE PARTICLE: the unit physics cannot split.
branches.cn: 粒子线：物理学拆不开的那个单位。

branches.en: THE BEGINNING: what school teaches and what everyone should know.
branches.cn: 起点线：学校所教，也是人人都该会的。

branches.en: THE MINIMUM: simple in a book, simple in matter.
branches.cn: 最小线：书里的简单，与物质里的简单。

intro.en: Elementary is element plus -ary, from Latin -arius, meaning belonging to; there is no prefix involved.
intro.cn: elementary 是 element 加 -ary，来自拉丁语 -arius，意为「属于」；这里不涉及任何前缀。

latinIntro.en: Elementum and elementarius are recorded Latin forms; the adjective entered English through French.
latinIntro.cn: elementum 与 elementarius 是有记录的拉丁语形式；这个形容词经法语进入英语。

items.example: It is the base of this word.
It drops -ary to give the noun.

items.meaningCN: 磨损的拉丁词尾，并非后缀
items.example: It belongs to element, not to a suffix.
items.exampleCN: 它属于 element 本身，不是后缀。

definition_zh: 举起；抬高；提高（水平、地位）；使（精神）振奋
definition_en: to lift something to a higher position, to raise a level or rank, or to lift someone's spirits
core_image: 一根木杠支在石头上，把沉重的一端缓缓顶起
scene: 工人们用一台旧升降架把一根横梁从地面吊到了墙顶。They elevated the beam to the top of the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 elevate 是「举起、抬高」（第 1 个义项：把物体移到更高的位置）；句意是他们把那根横梁吊到了墙顶。

pos.zh: 举起；抬高；提高；使振奋

senses.title: To lift something up
senses.definition: to raise a physical object to a higher place or position
senses.definitionCN: 把实物移到更高处的位置
senses.example: They elevated the beam to the top of the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把横梁吊到了墙顶。
senses.why: Latin levare meant to lighten, and lifting a heavy thing is exactly how you make it feel light, so e- plus levare became to raise.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 levare 意为「使变轻」，而举起重物正是让它显得轻的方式，于是 e- 加 levare 成了「举起」。

senses.title: To raise a level or rank
senses.definition: to increase the level, quality or rank of something abstract
senses.definitionCN: 提高抽象事物的水平、质量或地位
senses.example: The new policy elevated the status of rural teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策提高了乡村教师的地位。
senses.why: Height is the oldest picture of importance, so raising a number or a rank borrows the same upward motion.
senses.whyCN: 高度是最古老的表示重要性的图景，于是抬高数字或等级也借用同一个向上的动作。

senses.title: To lift the spirits
senses.definition: to make someone feel happier, nobler or more hopeful
senses.definitionCN: 使人更快乐、更高尚或更有希望
senses.example: The music elevated everyone's mood.
senses.exampleCN: 那音乐让所有人的情绪都振奋起来。
senses.why: A low mood is a low position, so cheering someone up is described as lifting them.
senses.whyCN: 低落的心情被看作低处，于是让一个人高兴起来就被说成把他举起。

senses.title: To promote in the church
senses.definition: in religious usage, to raise someone to a higher office, especially in the Catholic Church
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教用法中把某人提升到更高职位，尤指天主教会
senses.example: He was elevated to bishop last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他去年春天被擢升为主教。
senses.why: An office is a seat placed higher, so appointment to it is spoken of as being lifted up.
senses.whyCN: 职位被想象成摆得更高的座位，因此任命就被说成被举上去。

intro.en: Elevate is Latin e- (out, up) plus levare, to lighten or raise; here the e- really is a prefix from ex-, unlike the e- inside element.
intro.cn: elevate 是拉丁语 e-（向外、向上）加 levare（使轻、举起）；这里的 e- 确实来自 ex- 的前缀，与 element 内部的 e- 不同。

items.en: Levis meant light in weight, the opposite of heavy.
items.cn: levis 意为「轻的」，与「重」相对。

items.en: Levare meant to lighten, and by extension to lift or relieve.
items.cn: levare 意为「使变轻」，引申为举起、减轻。

items.en: Adding ex- gave elevare, to lift out and up.
items.cn: 加上 ex- 构成 elevare，意为「抬出去、举起来」。

items.en: Its past participle elevatus described something already raised.
items.cn: 其过去分词 elevatus 形容已被抬起之物。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century for physical lifting.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词，最初指物理上的抬起。

items.en: Rank, mood and church office all took the same upward picture.
items.cn: 等级、心情与教会职位都采用了同一个向上的图景。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the levare family; the near-meaning group separates raise, lift, promote and boost.
note.cn: 形近组收 levare 词族；近义组区分 raise、lift、promote 与 boost。

entries.definition: The machine that lifts people or goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电梯；升降机」，即负责举升的机器。

entries.definition: Height above sea level, or the act of raising.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海拔；提升」，指高出海平面的高度或抬起的动作。

entries.definition: Raised up, or noble in style.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「升高的；高雅的」。

entries.definition: A bar used to lift; from the same Latin verb levare.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杠杆」，与 elevate 同出拉丁语 levare。

entries.definition: The plain everyday verb for lifting; neutral in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「举起、提高」，最日常、语气中性。

entries.definition: To move something up, often with effort and by hand.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抬起」，常指费力地用手举起。

entries.definition: To move someone to a higher job; only the rank sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「晋升」，只对应本词的地位义。

entries.definition: To push a level or mood upward; informal and energetic.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提振、促进」，口语化，强调推力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks take the prefix literally: e- means up, levare means to lighten, so elevating is making heavy things feel light.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把前缀照字面读：e- 是向上，levare 是使轻，所以 elevate 就是让重的东西显得轻。

normal.en: E- is the prefix here, and it means up, out of the way.
normal.cn: 这里的 e- 确实是前缀，意思是向上、抬离原位。

normal.en: Lift a stone and it feels lighter; that is levare in action.
normal.cn: 把石头举起来，它就显得轻了，这就是 levare 在起作用。

normal.en: Elevate a number and it rises; elevate a rank and it climbs.
normal.cn: elevate 一个数字，它上升；elevate 一个等级，它爬高。

normal.en: Good news elevates the mood because joy is pictured as height.
normal.cn: 好消息能 elevate 情绪，因为喜悦被画成高处。

normal.en: Elevator is just elevate plus -or: the thing that lifts.
normal.cn: elevator 就是 elevate 加 -or：负责举升的那个东西。

abstract.en: Picture a lever under a boulder, the far end pressed down.
abstract.cn: 想象一根杠杆压在巨石下，远端被按下去。

abstract.en: The stone rises because the other end was made to feel light.
abstract.cn: 石头升起，是因为另一端被压得「轻」了。

abstract.en: Elevate is the moment when weight stops being the whole story.
abstract.cn: elevate 就是重量不再是全部故事的那一刻。

examples.en: They elevated the beam to the top of the wall.
examples.cn: 他们把横梁吊到了墙顶。

examples.en: The new policy elevated the status of rural teachers.
examples.cn: 新政策提高了乡村教师的地位。

examples.en: The music elevated everyone's mood.
examples.cn: 那音乐让所有人的情绪都振奋起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艾勒维特」——杠杆一压，沉重的石板就离地了

root: 源自拉丁语 elevare，由前缀 e-（＝ex-，向外、向上）加 levare（使轻、举起）构成；levare 出自 levis「轻的」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of elevate: lifting an object, raising a level or rank, lifting the spirits, and promotion to a church office.
sensesIntro.cn: elevate 的四个义项：举起实物、提高水平或地位、振奋情绪，以及教会中的擢升。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lever under a boulder, the far end pressed down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根杠杆垫在巨石下，远端被按下去。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: something moved to a higher place.
branches.cn: 实物线：被移到更高处的东西。

branches.en: THE LEVEL: numbers and ranks treated as heights.
branches.cn: 水平线：被当作高度的数字与等级。

branches.en: THE SPIRIT: a low mood lifted out of its hollow.
branches.cn: 情绪线：从低谷里被抬起来的心情。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: a seat that is higher than the last.
branches.cn: 职位线：比原来更高的一个座位。

branches.en: THE LEVER: the same motion works on stone and on rank.
branches.cn: 杠杆线：同一个动作既作用于石头，也作用于等级。

intro.en: Elevate is e- plus levare; the prefix here is the Latin ex-, meaning out or up, so the e- is genuine and means something.
intro.cn: elevate 是 e- 加 levare；这里的前缀是拉丁语 ex-，意为向外、向上，所以这个 e- 是真正的、有含义的前缀。

latinIntro.en: Levis, levare, elevare and elevatus are all recorded Latin forms; English took the verb through French.
latinIntro.cn: levis、levare、elevare 与 elevatus 都是有记录的拉丁语形式；英语经法语借入这个动词。

items.example: It is the deepest root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族最深的根。

items.example: It gives the English adjective elevated.
items.exampleCN: 它生出英语形容词 elevated。

definition_zh: 海拔；提高；高地；立面图；晋升；仰角
definition_en: the height of a place above sea level, or the act of raising something to a higher level
core_image: 一根测量杆从海平面被缓缓抬到山脊，刻度一路向上走
scene: 勘察队在山脚架好仪器，沿坡缓慢向上测量。Surveyors record the elevation of the ridge as two thousand metres.
sceneCN: 这里 elevation 指「某地高出海平面的海拔」（第 1 个义项：以海平面为基准量出的垂直高度）；句意为测量员记录这道山脊的海拔约为两千米。图中可辨识物件：水准仪、标尺、等高线地图、山脊。

pos.zh: 海拔；高度；提高；晋升；高地；（建筑的）立面图；仰角

senses.title: Height above sea level
senses.titleCN: 海拔：高出海平面的高度
senses.definition: the height of a place or object measured from sea level
senses.definitionCN: 某地或某物以海平面为基准量出的高度
senses.example: The village sits at an elevation of eighteen hundred metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子坐落在海拔一千八百米处。
senses.why: E- 'out, upward' plus levare 'to raise' gives 'a raising up'; measured from the sea, that raised distance is the elevation.
senses.whyCN: e-「向外、向上」加 levare「抬起」构成「被举起」；以海面为起点量这段被举起的高度，就是海拔。

senses.title: The act of raising something
senses.titleCN: 提高：把东西抬到更高处
senses.definition: the act or result of lifting something to a higher position
senses.definitionCN: 把某物抬到更高位置的动作或结果
senses.example: The elevation of the platform took three cranes.
senses.exampleCN: 把平台抬高用了三台起重机。
senses.why: The noun keeps the literal movement of the verb elevate: an object is moved upward.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词保留了动词 elevate 的字面动作：物体被向上移动。

senses.title: A raised piece of ground
senses.titleCN: 高地：高出周围地面的隆起
senses.definition: a hill or raised area of land standing above its surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 高出周围地面的小山或隆起地块
senses.example: The old church stands on a slight elevation above the marsh.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老教堂坐落在湿地上方一处略高的地方。
senses.why: A patch of land that has been raised, geologically or simply by contrast, is called an elevation because it stands above the flat ground.
senses.whyCN: 地块相对四周被抬高，无论成因如何，都因高出平地而被称为 elevation。

senses.title: Angle above the horizon
senses.titleCN: 仰角：视线在水平线以上的夹角
senses.definition: the angle between an object in the sky and the horizontal, measured upward
senses.definitionCN: 天空中某物体与水平面之间向上量出的夹角
senses.example: The astronomer measured the elevation of the star before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家在黎明前测量了那颗星的仰角。
senses.why: Surveying lifts a sight line from the level horizon toward a target, so the angle of that lift is also an elevation.
senses.whyCN: 测量时把视线从水平面向目标抬起，这条抬起的角度同样叫 elevation。

senses.title: Architectural facade drawing
senses.titleCN: 立面图：建筑外墙的正投影图
senses.definition: a scale drawing that shows the front or side of a building as seen straight on
senses.definitionCN: 从正面或侧面正对建筑画出的按比例图纸
senses.example: The architect sent the council a front elevation of the new library.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师向市政会提交了新图书馆的正立面图。
senses.why: The facade is drawn as if the building had been lifted and laid flat toward the viewer; French architectural usage gave this sense to English.
senses.whyCN: 立面图把建筑外表面「抬起、摊平」正对观者；这一义项经法语建筑用语进入英语。

senses.title: Promotion in rank or status
senses.titleCN: 晋升：地位被抬到更高一级
senses.definition: the act of raising someone to a higher rank, office or dignity
senses.definitionCN: 把某人提升到更高军衔、职位或地位的举动
senses.example: Her elevation to the board surprised no one.
senses.exampleCN: 她被提升进董事会，谁都不觉得意外。
senses.why: A person is metaphorically lifted from a lower place in a hierarchy to a higher one, so the same raising verb serves social rank.
senses.whyCN: 人被比喻性地从层级较低处抬到较高处，这个「抬起」动词因此也用于社会地位。

senses.title: Increase in amount or level
senses.titleCN: 升高：数值或强度的上升
senses.definition: an increase in the amount or intensity of something measured
senses.definitionCN: 某可测量事物在数量或强度上的上升
senses.example: Doctors watched the elevation of his blood pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 医生们关注着他血压的升高。
senses.why: A reading that climbs is a value raised above its earlier level, which extends the physical 'raise' to numbers.
senses.whyCN: 读数向上爬升，就是数值被抬到高于原先的水平，物理的「抬起」由此延伸到数字。

senses.title: Lofty quality of style or thought
senses.titleCN: 高远：文风或思想境界的提升
senses.definition: a dignified or noble quality in language, thought or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 语言、思想或情感中庄重崇高的品质
senses.example: The sermon was praised for the elevation of its language.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇布道因语言格调高远而受到称赞。
senses.why: The medieval religious sense of raising the mind toward higher things survives in talk about elevated style and thought.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪宗教语境中「把心灵引向更高之物」的用法，留存为今天说文体与思想「高远」。

intro.en: Elevation comes through French from Latin elevatio, a noun of action from elevare 'to raise'. The verb is built from a prefix of upward movement and a root meaning 'light, to lift'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: elevation 经法语来自拉丁 elevatio，是动词 elevare「举起」的动名词；该动词由表示向上移动的前缀与「轻、抬起」的词根构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Levare 'to lift, raise' was formed on levis 'light, not heavy'; lifting is what one does with something light. The link is generally accepted, while the deeper Indo-European source of levis is reconstructed as a 'light, nimble' root.
items.cn: levare「举起、抬起」由 levis「轻的、不重的」构成；轻的东西才容易被抬起。这一联系一般认为是可靠的，而 levis 在印欧语中更深的来源则属重构形式。

items.en: The prefix e- (from ex-) 'out, upward' plus levare produced elevare 'to raise up, lift, relieve'.
items.cn: 前缀 e-（源自 ex-）表示「向外、向上」，加 levare 构成 elevare「举起、抬高、减轻」。

items.en: Elevatio, elevationis (feminine, third declension) is the action noun: 'a lifting up, a raising'.
items.cn: elevatio（阴性，第三变格）是动作名词，意为「举起、抬高」。

items.en: Old French elevation carried both the physical and the religious sense of raising the mind; English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 elevation 同时带有物理上的「举起」与宗教上的「使心灵升华」两义；英语在 14 世纪借入。

items.en: The modern 'height above sea level' sense belongs to surveying and cartography from the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries; no precise first citation is recorded.
items.cn: 现代「高出海平面的高度」义属于 18 至 19 世纪的测量与制图学；确切的最早书证未见记载。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates only): the architectural sense of a facade drawing is attested later than the general noun, but its exact entry date in English is unsettled. The Latin root itself is not in doubt.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：立面图义晚于一般名词义出现，但其进入英语的确切年代无定论。拉丁词根本身并无争议。

note.en: Group one gathers words that look close to elevation; group two gathers words that also name a height but measure it differently.
note.cn: 第一组是外形与 elevation 接近的词；第二组是同样表示高度、但测量基准不同的词。

entries.definition: Elevate plus -or 'one that does': the machine that raises people or goods, not the height itself.
entries.definitionCN: elevate 加 -or「做某事者」：指把人或货抬起来的机器，而不是高度本身。

entries.definition: From Latin levis 'light' through levitas: the act of rising or floating, with no reference to a measured altitude.
entries.definitionCN: 经拉丁 levitas 来自 levis「轻」：指升空或悬浮，与量出的高度无关。

entries.definition: Ad- 'toward' plus levare 'lighten': to make pain or a burden lighter, not to raise a place.
entries.definitionCN: ad-「朝向」加 levare「使轻」：减轻痛苦或负担，而非把地方抬高。

entries.definition: From Latin efferre 'carry away, lift up' in the sense of spirits being carried high; it is a feeling, not a height.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 efferre「带走、举起」中「情绪被抬高」的用法；指心情，不指高度。

entries.definition: The vertical height of an object or aircraft above a chosen level; elevation usually measures land against sea level.
entries.definitionCN: 物体或飞机高出某一选定基准的垂直高度；elevation 通常指陆地相对海平面的高度。

entries.definition: The everyday word for how tall or how high something is, with no technical baseline.
entries.definitionCN: 日常用词，指某物有多高，不含技术性的基准面。

entries.definition: A mass of rock pushed upward by forces inside the earth; it names the process, while elevation can name the resulting height.
entries.definitionCN: 地壳内力把岩体向上推；它指过程，而 elevation 可指结果的高度。

entries.definition: A simple increase in level or position; elevation is the measured or formal result of such a rise.
entries.definitionCN: 指水平或位置的简单上升；elevation 是这种上升被测量或正式记录的结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real surveying terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的语素、真实的测量术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: E- 'up, out' + levare 'lift': the height you get after lifting a point above sea level.
normal.cn: e-「向上、向外」+ levare「抬起」：把一个点抬到海平面之上得到的高度。

normal.en: The lever and levitate family share the 'lift, light' idea, so elevation belongs with things that rise.
normal.cn: lever 与 levitate 同带「抬起、轻」的意思，因此 elevation 与「上升」一类概念同族。

normal.en: Hikers speak of elevation gain, the total climbing on a route.
normal.cn: 徒步者说 elevation gain，指一条路线累计爬升的总高度。

normal.en: In maps, elevation is measured against sea level; in flight, the same idea is usually called altitude.
normal.cn: 地图上的 elevation 以海平面为基准；飞行中同一概念通常叫 altitude。

normal.en: An architect's elevation is a flat drawing of a facade, seen straight on rather than from above.
normal.cn: 建筑师的 elevation 是立面的平面图，正对墙面看，而不是从上往下看。

abstract.en: Picture a stage lift carrying a speaker up into the light.
abstract.cn: 想象一台舞台升降机把演讲者抬到灯光里。

abstract.en: Picture a hill that is only a hill because the plain around it stays low.
abstract.cn: 想象一座山丘之所以是山丘，只因四周平原保持低矮。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence whose tone is lifted a register above ordinary speech.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话的语气比日常说话高出一个音区。

examples.en: The trail climbs to an elevation of three thousand metres.
examples.cn: 这条步道爬升到海拔三千米。

examples.en: A front elevation shows the building as a flat pattern of windows and doors.
examples.cn: 正立面图把建筑呈现为门窗排列的平面图案。

examples.en: His elevation to captain came after ten years of service.
examples.cn: 服役十年后，他被晋升为上尉。

dict_mnemonic.text: e（向外、向上）+ lev（举起，如 lever 杠杆）+ ation（名词）→ 被举起来的高度 → 海拔、提升

root: 拉丁 elevare「举起」= e-（向外、向上）+ levare「抬起」；levare 源于 levis「轻」。英语 elevation 经法语借入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: a point, a value or a person is lifted above a base line, and the result of that lift is the elevation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把一个点、一个数值或一个人抬到基准线之上，抬起的结果就是 elevation。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surveyor's rod lifted from sea level to a ridge, reading the vertical rise.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根测量杆从海平面被抬到山脊，读出这段垂直上升。

branches.en: MEASURE UP: from sea level or from the horizon, both senses give a number for height above a base.
branches.cn: 向上量：无论以海平面还是以水平线为基准，两个义项都给出高出基准的数值。

branches.en: INCREASE: raising an object and raising a value are the same upward movement seen in space and in numbers.
branches.cn: 上升：抬起物体与抬升数值，是空间与数字中同一个向上动作。

branches.en: GROUND: when the rise belongs to land, the result stands as a hill.
branches.cn: 地面：当上升属于土地，结果就立成一座高地。

branches.en: FORM: a facade is a building lifted onto flat paper; elevated style is language lifted above the ordinary.
branches.cn: 形式：立面图是把建筑抬到纸面上；高远的文风是把语言抬到日常之上。

branches.en: RANK: a person is lifted to a higher place in a hierarchy.
branches.cn: 位阶：人被抬到层级中更高的位置。

intro.en: Elevation is a Latin noun of action whose prefix, root and suffix all recur in English words, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: elevation 是拉丁动作名词，其前缀、词根与后缀都在英语其它词中复现，因此这个词族可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin levare 'to lift' yields elevate, elevation, elevator and alleviate, while levis 'light' also gives levity and levitation; ex- adds the upward direction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 levare「举起」衍生 elevate、elevation、elevator 与 alleviate；levis「轻」还衍生 levity 与 levitation；ex- 增添向上的方向。

items.example: The prefix turns the root into a movement away from the ground.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把词根变成离开地面的动作。

items.example: The root supplies the physical lift.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供物理上的抬起。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into the name of its result.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把动词变成其结果的名称。

items.example: The ridge's elevation was marked on the map.
items.exampleCN: 这道山脊的海拔被标在地图上。

items.example: The elevator rose to the top floor.

items.exampleCN: 他的轻率惹恼了委员会。

items.example: The trick appeared to produce levitation.
items.exampleCN: 这个戏法看起来像让人悬浮。

definition_zh: 电梯；升降机；升降舵；谷物提升机
definition_en: a machine in a building that carries people or goods between floors, a movable flap on an aircraft tail, or a machine that lifts grain
core_image: 金属轿厢沿着一列井道灯缓缓上升，楼层数字一格一格跳
scene: 酒店大堂里，穿制服的服务生替客人按住门，轿厢稳稳停住。The elevator stopped at the fourteenth floor.
sceneCN: 这里 elevator 是「电梯」（第 1 个义项：在楼层之间运送人或货的机器）；句意是电梯停在了十四层。

pos.zh: 电梯；升降机；升降舵；谷物提升机

senses.title: A machine between floors
senses.definition: a cage or platform in a building that carries people or goods up and down between floors
senses.definitionCN: 建筑中在楼层之间运送人或货的轿厢或平台
senses.example: The elevator stopped at the fourteenth floor.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯停在了十四层。
senses.why: The -or ending names the thing that does the verb, so elevator is literally the lifter, and the machine that lifts became the word.
senses.whyCN: -or 词尾命名做这个动作的东西，所以 elevator 字面就是「举升者」，负责举升的机器便得了这个名字。

senses.title: A flap on the tail
senses.definition: a hinged control surface on the tailplane of an aircraft that makes the nose go up or down
senses.definitionCN: 飞机水平尾翼上可转动的操纵面，使机头抬起或低下
senses.example: The pilot pushed the elevator down and the nose dropped.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员推下升降舵，机头随即下沉。
senses.why: The flap literally lifts or lowers the nose, so aviation reused the same agent noun for the part that does it.
senses.whyCN: 这块舵面确实在抬起或压低机头，于是航空业把同一个施动名词用在了做这件事的部件上。

senses.title: A grain lifter
senses.definition: a tall building or machine that lifts and stores grain in bulk
senses.definitionCN: 把谷物大批提升并储存的高塔或机械
senses.example: The grain was trucked to the elevator beside the railway.
senses.exampleCN: 谷物被卡车运到铁路旁的谷物提升机。
senses.why: Farm machinery needed a plain name for a machine that raises grain, and the oldest sense of lift fitted exactly.
senses.whyCN: 农业机械需要给「把谷物举高」的机器一个朴素名称，而 lift 最古老的含义正合适。

intro.en: Elevator is elevate plus the Latin agent ending -or, so it means the lifter; American English applied it to the machine, while British English kept lift.
intro.cn: elevator 是 elevate 加拉丁语施动词尾 -or，意为「举升者」；美式英语把它用在机器上，英式英语则保留 lift。

items.en: Levare meant to lighten and to raise, built on levis, light in weight.
items.cn: levare 意为使轻、举起，其根是 levis（轻的）。

items.en: With the prefix ex- it became elevare, to lift up and out.
items.cn: 加上前缀 ex- 后成为 elevare，意为向上抬起。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词。

items.en: The agent ending -or made a noun meaning one that lifts.
items.cn: 施动词尾 -or 造出意为「举升者」的名词。

items.en: American English fixed the word on the passenger machine in tall buildings.
items.cn: 美式英语把这个词固定给高层建筑里的载人机器。

items.en: British lift and American elevator now name the same box, and aviation took the word for a tail flap.
items.cn: 英式 lift 与美式 elevator 如今指同一只轿厢，航空业又借它命名尾翼舵面。

note.en: The look-alike group links the elevate family; the near-meaning group separates lift, escalator and hoist.
note.cn: 形近组串起 elevate 词族；近义组区分 lift、escalator 与 hoist。

entries.definition: The verb that the noun is built from.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「举起；提高」，是本词的基干。

entries.definition: Height above sea level, or the act of raising.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海拔；提升」。

entries.definition: Raised, or noble in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「升高的；高雅的」。

entries.definition: A bar for lifting, from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杠杆」，与 elevator 同根。

entries.definition: The British word for the same machine; also a general verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电梯」，是英式说法，也可作一般动词。

entries.definition: A moving staircase, not a box; it carries you step by step.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自动扶梯」，是移动的楼梯而非轿厢。

entries.definition: A rope or machine for lifting heavy loads, usually outdoors.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「起重机、卷扬机」，多用于室外吊重物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks read the word as lift plus the doer, then follow that doer into a shaft, a tail and a grain tower.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把词读成「举起＋做这事的东西」，再让这个「做者」走进井道、机尾与谷仓塔。

normal.en: Elevate plus -or: the thing that lifts.
normal.cn: elevate 加 -or：负责举升的那个东西。

normal.en: In Britain the same box is simply called a lift.
normal.cn: 在英国，同一只轿厢就直接叫 lift。

normal.en: An elevator pitch is short enough to finish between floors.
normal.cn: elevator pitch 短到能在楼层之间讲完。

normal.en: On a plane the elevator lifts the nose, not the cabin.
normal.cn: 飞机上的 elevator 抬起的是机头，不是客舱。

normal.en: A grain elevator lifts wheat into a tower.
normal.cn: grain elevator 把小麦提升进高塔。

abstract.en: Picture a small metal room that refuses to stay on one floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小金属房间，就是不肯停在同一层。

abstract.en: The same name serves a tail flap and a grain tower, because all three raise something.
abstract.cn: 同一个名字兼指尾翼舵面与谷物塔，因为三者都在抬高什么。

abstract.en: Elevator is the verb elevate given a body.
abstract.cn: elevator 就是动词 elevate 被赋予了一具身体。

examples.en: The elevator stopped at the fourteenth floor.
examples.cn: 电梯停在了十四层。

examples.en: The pilot pushed the elevator down and the nose dropped.
examples.cn: 飞行员推下升降舵，机头随即下沉。

examples.en: The grain was trucked to the elevator beside the railway.
examples.cn: 谷物被卡车运到铁路旁的谷物提升机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艾勒维特」——轿厢一升，楼层数字就跳一格

root: 由 elevate 加拉丁语施动词尾 -or 构成，字面意为「举升者」；elevate 出自 elevare，即前缀 e-（＝ex-）加 levare「使轻、举起」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of elevator: the machine in a building, the tail flap of an aircraft, and the machine that lifts grain.
sensesIntro.cn: elevator 的三个义项：建筑里的电梯、飞机的升降舵，以及提升谷物的机械。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a metal box climbing a shaft, floor numbers ticking upward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只金属轿厢沿井道上升，楼层数字一跳一跳。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: people and goods moving between floors.
branches.cn: 建筑线：在楼层之间运送人与货。

branches.en: THE AIRCRAFT: a flap that tilts the nose.
branches.cn: 航空线：让机头俯仰的舵面。

branches.en: THE FARM: grain raised into a tower.
branches.cn: 农业线：把谷物提升进高塔。

branches.en: THE LIFT: a shaft for people and a shaft for wheat.
branches.cn: 举升线：送人的井道与送麦的塔都叫这个名字。

branches.en: THE CONTROL: one is controlled by buttons, one by a stick.
branches.cn: 操控线：一个靠按钮，一个靠操纵杆。

intro.en: Elevator is elevate plus the Latin agent ending -or, so its shape says one that lifts; the e- inside elevate is the real prefix ex-.
intro.cn: elevator 是 elevate 加拉丁语施动词尾 -or，字形本身就在说「举升者」；elevate 内部的 e- 是真正的前缀 ex-。

latinIntro.en: Levare and elevare are recorded Latin verbs; the agent noun elevator is a later English formation.
latinIntro.cn: levare 与 elevare 是有记录的拉丁语动词；施动名词 elevator 则是后来英语的构造。
